svg.title: Energy resources
svg.desc: Fossil & nuclear fuels: Coal, oil, gas and nuclear fuels are finite. Fossil fuels support heating, electricity and transport. Burning fossil fuels releases CO₂ and pollutants. Nuclear: reliable electricity, low operational CO₂, radioactive waste. Costs beyond fuel: Extraction damages habitats. Nuclear plants need expensive construction/decommissioning. Biofuel can regrow, but uses land and releases CO₂ when burned. Carbon balance depends on regrowth and production. Wind, Sun & waves: No fuel combustion during operation, but output varies with weather. Solar also varies with daylight. Wind: visual/noise/wildlife concerns. Waves: harsh conditions and maintenance. Solar: area and siting matter. Water & Earth: Hydro reservoirs can supply on demand but flood land; drought reduces supply. Tides are predictable, not continuous; estuary impacts. Geothermal is steady at suitable sites, with drilling costs. Match supply to use: Heating, transport and electricity have different needs. Use a mix, storage and flexible backup. Renewable means replenished as used; it does not mean always available or impact-free. Use evidence: Compare power, reliability, cost, emissions, waste and habitats. Justify which matters most. Read totals and percentage shares carefully. Scientific evidence cannot alone settle political or economic choices.
